item.title: Lae church launches reconstruction work two years after disaster
item.description: The Cassowary United Church in Lae, Morobe, has officially launched ground-filling works to reclaim its premises two years after part of its property was destroyed by natural disaster. The church's backyard was washed away by the flooding Bumbu River in August 2024, forcing the congregation to spend two years raising funds to restore the land.
item.content:encoded:
The Cassowary United Church in Lae, Morobe, has officially launched ground-filling works to reclaim its premises two years after part of its property was destroyed by natural disaster.

The church's backyard was washed away by the flooding Bumbu River in August 2024, forcing the congregation to spend two years raising funds to restore the land.

While other centers have celebrated progress, the Cassowary congregation was left to focus on land recovery efforts, ruling out any plans to relocate due to severe land scarcity in Lae.

Speaking during the ground-breaking ceremony, Reverend Rau Vetali expressed deep gratitude to church partners and stakeholders who supported their fundraising drives over the last two years.

“The church conducted two major fundraising dinners, one in Port Moresby and the other here in Lae, and we are still continuing,” Rev Vetali said.

“We are grateful for good support from the provincial administration and the former late Governor Luther Wenge.”

Several business houses in the province have also stepped in to contribute to the backfilling and land reclamation project.

Rev Vetali re-emphasized that the church would not move from its original site, though secondary operations have been shifted out of necessity.

“Land is scarce these days, but we would only source land elsewhere for other church activities,” he said.

“For example, our church-run elementary school has been relocated to a new site at this time.”

The ground-breaking ceremony coincided with a dual celebration marking the church's 57th anniversary alongside United Church congregations across the country.

Meanwhile, backfilling work started last week.

item.title: New Wapulaka Junior High double classroom nears completion
item.description: Construction of a new double classroom at Wapulaka Junior High School in Magarima, Hela, is scheduled for completion later this month. The project fully supported by a K200,000 allocation from the Magarima District Development Authority [DDA], is designed to relieve overcrowded learning spaces and improve conditions for students.
item.content:encoded:
Construction of a new double classroom at Wapulaka Junior High School in Magarima, Hela, is scheduled for completion later this month.

The project fully supported by a K200,000 allocation from the Magarima District Development Authority [DDA], is designed to relieve overcrowded learning spaces and improve conditions for students.

Speaking to NBC News, Magarima DDA chief executive officer Simon Olaija reaffirmed the authority's commitment to advancing local learning facilities.

​"Education remains one of our top priorities," Olaija said. "The K200,000 allocated for this double classroom at Wapulaka Junior High is part of our ongoing effort to upgrade school infrastructure throughout the district." ​ ​He said the project is part of a much broader, long-term initiative. Even prior to recent administrative shifts, when the body functioned as the Komo-Magarima DDA, the authority consistently funded the construction of classrooms and staff housing across the district.

​The CEO also expressed gratitude towards the provincial government for targeting teacher accommodation, a persistent issue that affected teachers.

​"On behalf of the DDA, I want to sincerely thank Hela Governor Philip Undialu for funding vital infrastructure, particularly the 8-in-1 staff housing units," Olaija said.

"Housing has long been a major barrier. Delivering proper living quarters allows our teachers to settle in securely and focus entirely on providing quality education to our students."

​He emphasized that the pioneer Magarima Secondary School continues to receive sustained financial backing from the DDA.

This ongoing support aims to expand facility capacity and modernise resources to accommodate the district's steadily growing student population.

item.title: Three agencies join forces to bring fire service to Hela
item.description: A tripartite Memorandum of Understanding [MOU] has been signed to establish Hela’s first permanent emergency fire response service in Tari. The agreement, signed between the Hela Provincial Government [HPG], the National Airports Corporation [NAC], and the Papua New Guinea Fire Service [PNGFS], will see the province receive its first dedicated fire truck.
item.content:encoded:
A tripartite Memorandum of Understanding [MOU] has been signed to establish Hela’s first permanent emergency fire response service in Tari.

The agreement, signed between the Hela Provincial Government [HPG], the National Airports Corporation [NAC], and the Papua New Guinea Fire Service [PNGFS], will see the province receive its first dedicated fire truck.

The new station will provide critical fire and emergency coverage for Tari airport and township, local commercial centers, and surrounding communities.

Hela Governor Philip Undialu welcomed the signing, stating that it is an essential step towards protecting the province’s major infrastructure boom and increasing air traffic.

Tari Airport currently handles up to 12 flights a week.

“NAC, the National Government, and private investors have poured hundreds of millions of kina into public and private infrastructure across Hela,” Undialu said.

“Establishing a permanent fire service is essential to protecting these investments and creating greater confidence for future development.”

Under the terms of the MoU: representatives from HPG, NAC, and PNGFS will conduct a site inspection within 60 days to finalize designs for the permanent fire station; the PNGFS will deploy a Commanding Officer to be stationed in Tari to direct local emergency operations once active; and, all three entities will jointly co-fund and develop the necessary fire service infrastructure.

Signatories to the agreement included NAC board chairman Jacob Anga, acting managing director Dominic Kaumi, PNGFS representative Commander Bill Hoo, governor Undialu, and Hela provincial administrator Ronny Angu.

Undialu extended his appreciation to the partner agencies, saying that the multi-agency framework serves as a benchmark for government collaboration aimed at building a safer and more resilient Hela.

item.title: Simbu health services scaled down as El Niño affects water and essential supplies
item.description: The Simbu Provincial Health Authority and the Simbu Catholic Health Services have announced a temporary reduction in health services across the province, citing the worsening effects of El Niño on water supply, food security, and other essential resources needed to sustain normal operations. The decision affects health facilities under both organizations, which say the continued dry conditions hav
item.content:encoded:
The Simbu Provincial Health Authority and the Simbu Catholic Health Services have announced a temporary reduction in health services across the province, citing the worsening effects of El Niño on water supply, food security, and other essential resources needed to sustain normal operations.

The decision affects health facilities under both organizations, which say the continued dry conditions have placed pressure on health service delivery and forced them to prioritize the most urgent and life-saving care.

Similar drought-related concerns have been reported across Simbu in recent weeks, with communities facing water shortages and declining food gardens.

SiPHA chief executive officer Dr Kassi Ken and Bishop Paul Sindu of the Kundiawa Catholic Diocese said the adjustment is necessary to protect essential services while resources remain constrained.

Dr. Ken said the move is aimed at ensuring that frontline health workers can continue providing care in the areas of greatest need.

"Under the new arrangement, only critical services will continue. These include emergency care, maternal and child health services, and urgent outpatient treatment. Routine clinics, outreach programs, and other non-essential services will be temporarily reduced until conditions improve," he said

Bishop Sindu also said the decision was made with regret but was necessary to maintain service continuity during the current hardship.

He thanked health workers, church partners, and communities for their understanding and cooperation as facilities adjust to the ongoing drought-related impacts.

They urged the public to use available services responsibly and to work closely with health workers during this period of reduced operations.

The two organizations said they remain committed to serving the people of Simbu and will restore normal services once conditions improve.

item.title: Asigi people call for restoration of basic services in Sohe
item.description: Residents of Asigi in Sohe, Northern, are calling for the urgent restoration of basic government services to their area following severe disruption to their livelihoods over the past three years. Community members highlighted their plight during a joint stakeholder awareness campaign conducted at Papoga, Kanari, and Jajau villages recently.
item.content:encoded:
Residents of Asigi in Sohe, Northern, are calling for the urgent restoration of basic government services to their area following severe disruption to their livelihoods over the past three years.

Community members highlighted their plight during a joint stakeholder awareness campaign conducted at Papoga, Kanari, and Jajau villages recently.

The community has been struggling to rebuild since 2023, when lawlessness and civil unrest left numerous families displaced and without steady income sources.

A multi-agency team comprising officials from the Oil Palm Industry Corporation [OPIC], Higaturu Oil Palm’s smallholder affairs department, Popondetta Oil Palm Growers Association executives, the Oro provincial government, and Mobile Squad 20 officers, visited the area to address security and development concerns.

The delegation pledged to assist the community through targeted rehabilitation and restoration programs, but stressed that development hinged on total cooperation from locals.

Opic project manager Keuva Kiniawe urged residents to prioritize community peace, stating that basic services and economic opportunities could not survive in an unstable environment.

“Improving livelihoods can only happen if law and order is established first,” Kiniawe said.

Representatives from Higaturu and Mobile Squad 20 also appealed to Asigi leaders and youth to work alongside law enforcement to ensure lasting peace so service providers could safely return to the district.

Their plea for return of basic government services follows the criminal activities orchestrated by the Don't Care gang which affected the Asigi community three years ago.

item.title: NBC gives illegal squatters 21 days to vacate property
item.description: The National Broadcasting Corporation [NBC] has given illegal squatters residing behind the 5 Mile headquarters in Port Moresby 21 days to leave the property or face eviction by police. The victim was taken to hospital and the family has reported the matter t
item.content:encoded:
The National Broadcasting Corporation [NBC] has given illegal squatters residing behind the 5 Mile headquarters in Port Moresby 21 days to leave the property or face eviction by police.

Managing Director Kora Nou made the announcement today following an alleged attack on the son of a senior NBC staff member over the weekend. The victim was taken to hospital and the family has reported the matter to police.

Mr Nou said NBC has started discussions with the Metropolitan Superintendent, and police officers will begin awareness with the squatters so they can voluntarily move out within the next 21 days.

“Failure to do so will result in NBC requesting the Courts and police to evict them.” Mr Nou said

He also called on the squatters to identify those responsible for the attack and hand them over to police for investigation.

“May I remind everyone that the officers of the NBC throughout the country provide an essential service to our people every day, on weekends, and public holidays.

“These officers and their families do not deserve such unprovoked physical attacks or daily intimidation as they carry out their work, especially within the confines of our institutional housing premises.

“Harassment, physical attacks and unruly drunken behaviour in the vicinity of our 5 Mile staff residences have also increased since more illegal settlers have moved in from eviction exercises in other parts of Port Moresby.

“We will work with the Courts, the police, and NCDC to immediately stop this, as well we remove the illegal squatters already there,” Mr Nou

Mr Nou said the eviction is also part of NBC's plans to develop the land. Funding has already been secured to build 38 new staff houses at the 5 Mile site, with construction expected to begin once a building permit is issued.

He said the land currently occupied by the illegal squatters is needed for the new housing project.

item.title: Governor Bird responds to Angoram boundary concern
item.description: East Sepik Governor Allan Bird has responded to concerns raised by communities in Angoram over the new Middle Sepik electoral boundary, saying the matter is now being addressed in consultation with relevant government agencies. The Governor's response was posted on his official Facebook page on Saturday, 1st August following concerns raised by the Kanda communities over the inclusion of parts of t
item.content:encoded:
East Sepik Governor Allan Bird has responded to concerns raised by communities in Angoram over the new Middle Sepik electoral boundary, saying the matter is now being addressed in consultation with relevant government agencies.

The Governor's response was posted on his official Facebook page on Saturday, 1st August following concerns raised by the Kanda communities over the inclusion of parts of their customary land into the newly created Middle Sepik District.

In the Facebook statement, Governor Bird wrote, "The decision on the boundaries were made around 2021." He added that he had been informed a public consultation meeting was held at Sir Michael Somare Stadium in Wewak before the boundary decision was finalised.

According to the Governor, the East Sepik Provincial Government only received the final boundary decision in January this year. It was then that the province realised Angoram Station had been placed within the new district.

"We took a decision in 2023 to split Angoram Local Level Government into two so Angoram township will remain in Angoram District because ESPG has already decided to build the new district headquarters in Timbunke," the statement reads.

The Governor also acknowledged the legal challenges involved, stating, "We have been informed that we may be legally out of time." A technical team was established four weeks ago to work with the Department of Provincial and Local Government Affairs and other relevant agencies to resolve the boundary issues.

Governor Bird believes the situation could have been avoided had the Provincial Government been consulted during the 2021 boundary review.

"Had ESPG been consulted in 2021, the current issues would have been avoided," he wrote.

The Governor also assured the people of Angoram that they would be kept informed as discussions continue.

"I will inform our people in Angoram as to the outcomes of the consultations with relevant agencies once completed," Governor Bird wrote.

item.title: East Sepik holds tribute service for Rabaul boat tragedy victims
item.description: The East Sepik community gathered on Saturday to honor and remember the 27 lives lost in the recent tragic boat incident in Rabaul, East New Britain Province. A tribute mass was held on Saturday evening, 1st August 2026, at Marist beach, where men, women and children gathered to to pay their respects.
item.content:encoded:
The East Sepik community gathered on Saturday to honor and remember the 27 lives lost in the recent tragic boat incident in Rabaul, East New Britain Province.

A tribute mass was held on Saturday evening, 1st August 2026, at Marist beach, where men, women and children gathered to to pay their respects.

The service was conducted by Father Bernard Burite from Christ the King Church, Wiruwi Parish, and Reverend Robert Heni from Wewak United Church.

During the prayer for the victims, Reverend Heni reminded the congregation that life is uncertain and encouraged people to dedicate their lives to God.

“As we dedicate the 27 lives lost, please remember us who are alive on earth. May this tribute also remind those of us who are living that only God knows the future, and that we must always dedicate our lives to Him in everything we do,” Reverend Heni said.

Following the service, lanterns were raised into the night sky, while 27 wreaths were laid on the sea as a symbol of remembrance for each of the lives lost in the tragedy.

The solemn tribute brought together families, children and community members who gathered along the Wewak shoreline in prayer, reflection and solidarity with those affected by the incident.

The glowing lanterns above the shoreline and the wreaths placed on the sea marked a powerful moment of remembrance, as the East Sepik community joined the nation in mourning and honoring the victims of the Rabaul boat tragedy.

item.title: Ipatas is urging the national government to strengthen policing in Enga
item.description: Enga Governor Sir Peter Ipatas has called on the National Government to strengthen policing in the province, saying lasting peace depends on a well-resourced police force.

item.description: It's been a month since the appointment of Electoral Commissioner Dr Nicole Haley to oversee election operations ahead of the 2027 general elections.
